correctness.rationale: Independent central edge coordinates give one equation a_i b_j−a_j b_i=0 per edge. On the support, ratios b_i/a_i are constant and free on each connected component; outside it, precisely the neighbors of the support must vanish. All m central coordinates are free, giving both the claimed dimension and rank by rank–nullity, including zero vertices and characteristic two. Multiplication by q^m(q−1)^|S| gives the rank enumerator. For the ordered pair of vertex-coordinate vectors, use the support of the nonzero two-coordinate columns instead: edge determinants vanish exactly when a component shares a projective line, with q+1 choices per component and q−1 amplitudes per vertex. This yields the stated specialization of Q and its normalization. The forest recurrence distinguishes zero from one fixed line at the root, correctly allowing only the same line or zero under a nonzero parent. Independent direct enumeration over F_3 checked every individual centralizer size on P_3, K_3, two disjoint edges, and C_4, with vertex-coordinate commuting totals 153, 105, 1089, 417, respectively. The supplied checker was read, not run; its recorded finite output is corroborative only.
residual_risks: The edge equations require independent central edge generators, not shared labels. The forest complexity counts arithmetic operations, not bit operations.

originality.rationale: Rossmann (2022) computes the exact fixed-support cokernel dimension for the transpose of this same adjoint matrix over every field. Adding the central coordinates and summing support multiplicities directly recover the claimed centralizers and rank enumerator. His class-count formula together with the equivalence of group and Lie commutation already determines the exact ordered commuting count. The Q notation is a re-expression of that count via an established weighted-coloring model; it does not rescue the asserted new explicit evaluation.
residual_risks: Rossmann uses adjacency modules and class numbers instead of Q notation; the verified equivalence is by the explicit row-space and count translations, not title matching.
